source_facts.statement: Opcode family syntax is declared as 'xor.type d, a, b;' with type alternatives including .pred, .b16, .b32, .b64.
Section prose defines operation as bitwise XOR; Semantics block states 'd = a ^ b;'.
Operands must match in size, but not necessarily in type; predicate types are allowed for this family.
The xor section is introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.
The xor family is supported on all target architectures.
Examples in this section include 'xor.b32  d,q,r;' and 'xor.b16  d,x,0x0001;'.
Section 9.7 says all PTX instructions may be predicated and may omit guard from syntax in instruction-description form.
Section 9.3 defines optional guard prefix @{!}p where absence means unconditional execution; guard controls conditional execution.
Result-producing instructions use operands d, a, b and may have optional bit-bucket '_' as destination in general PTX syntax.
Fundamental types are basic-type + width specifiers; .b16 is among bit-size specifiers.

derived_interpretations.statement: The bounded unit form is 'xor.b16 d, a, b;'.
Instruction computes a bitwise exclusive-or of operand bits: write-back value is d := (a ^ b) over the .b16 value width.
Predicate guard is optional and may be absent (unconditional), @p (execute when p is true), or @!p (execute when p is false).
Execution reads a and b and writes d on execute in this bounded model.
